en.html:
Kageaki"A hunting dog, then."
Sorimachi"Heh..."
Kageaki"The Clive Cannon chose you. Is that it? Once inside Aizu, a Yamato man could move about without the Sasagawa army taking too much notice..."
Kageaki"Getting inside is another matter. Without reliable credentials, who crosses that border now? Or does a Rokuhara hireling's name still command such respect?"
Sorimachi"Respect? At present, even for warding off bad luck it would be a useless charm..."
Sorimachi"Complete encirclement, they call it. Such a grand arrangement. But where is the wall? Only soldiers with guns, walking here and there... Look properly, and a gap will be there..."
Sorimachi"And if it is not there, make one. That is all."
Kageaki"............Did your master permit that?"
Kageaki"Did he not tell you to leave uninvolved people unharmed?"
Sorimachi"Certainly, certainly... He attached the words 'as far as possible.'"
Sorimachi"Now, if it proves impossible, impossible it is. What can be done...?"
Kageaki"..."
Sorimachi"Kheh, heh! Lieutenant Colonel Cannon is not confused on this point... Give an order like that, and somebody is bound to die. He knows very well."
Sorimachi"Knowing it, understanding it—still he gives the order. Afterwards, therefore, no sitting about with regrets and lamentations..."
Sorimachi"Not like you."
Kageaki"........................"
Kageaki"He would go that far... for me—"
Kageaki"For eliminating Captain Ootori and myself, he will go to these lengths? There is persistence for you."

雪車町 「無ければ無いで、開ければ・・・・いいだけの事で」
景明 「…………。 　お前の飼い主はそれを許したのか」

雪車町 「可能でなけりゃ、仕方ありません……」

en.html:
His provocations were not entitled to an answer. I loosened my knees and lowered my center a little.
What could the enemy attack with? That was the question requiring attention.

Sorimachi had his cane, and inside it, one blade. Nothing more.
No armor. To take him with my bare hands would be difficult; impossible, it should not be.

...And if it became necessary, Muramasa was there. Against this man I should practice chivalry? Even my own admiration would not be forthcoming.

すらなりはしない。

en.html:
Sorimachi was fast on his feet.
His heart and lungs, going by his appearance, ought to have been unhealthy. On what arrangement they were permitting this speed, I could not understand at once.

To close the gap was difficult.
He was not getting further ahead. Very good—but we could not go on like this.

Somewhere ahead should be the carriage with the Sasagawa Kubo's soldiers.
Let him enter that, and a simple pursuit would no longer remain simple.

If Chamberlain Nagakura's account was right, these were rear personnel without much fighting spirit. I could hardly suppose Sorimachi meant to set them against me.
Even so, trouble was certain.

I ought to catch him before that. Ought to—but...

雪車町は人並みを凌ぐ俊足だ。
　容色からして不健全に違いなかろう彼の心肺機能が
何故あの速度を許すのか、<ruby>俄<rt>にわ</rt></ruby>かには理解し難い。

　差を詰めるのは困難だった。
　引き離されこそしないが――このままでは不味い。

　おそらくこの先には篠川公方府の軍兵を乗せた車両
がある。
　その中に入られては、追うに追えなくなる。

　永倉侍従が言った、士気の低い後方要員という話が
本当なら、彼らと俺をかち合わせるところに雪車町の
意図があるとも思えないが。
　そんな事態になれば面倒であるのは間違いない。

　今のうちに捕まえるべきだ――が……

en.html:
At last I understood what had happened.
For understanding why, this was no help at all.

What result was he expecting?
My carriage, with the Ootori pair aboard, had been cut off from the locomotive. It was gradually losing speed. Granted. And then?

An inconvenience, certainly. A fatal predicament, by no means.
For what purpose this child's prank?

On a steep incline, with another locomotive coming up behind us, we might have slipped back into a dreadful collision. But neither condition applied.

Peaceful, level country. Another bridge just ahead.
Sorimachi's carriages had gained speed—perhaps by leaving ours behind—and were already halfway across it.

...The bridge was safe.
For proof, there was the man who had arranged the whole affair, crossing it himself.

After crossing, he surely did not propose to destroy it. For that, a considerable quantity of explosives would be required, or a gun. Neither was in sight.

I could not understand.
...Understanding or no understanding, destruction was coming closer. That much I could hear.

The train ahead completed its crossing.
In its place, the ours approached the bridge.

Nothing happened.
Sorimachi did nothing.

Only raised his arm lightly.
Toward the sky————

ja.html:
ようやくに現状事態を把握し。
　そして俺の困惑は更に深まった。

　こんな事をする意図が計り知れない。
　俺と大鳥主従が乗った車両は機関車から切り離され、
徐々に速度を落としている――だから、何なのか。

　不都合には違いないが、全く致命的な窮地とは言え
ない。
　何故……こんな、子供の悪戯のような真似を？

　今がまさに急勾配の坂道を登っている最中で、後方
からは別の機関車が迫っているような時でもあったの
なら、この列車は滑落したすえ凄惨な衝突事故を起こ
したことであろうが。そんな状況ではないのだ。

　列車はのどかな平地を走り抜け、再び橋に差し掛か
ろうとするところだった。
　先行する雪車町らの車両は、こちらを捨てたせいか
速度を増し、既に橋の半ばまで達している。

　……橋は安全だ。
　この状況を仕組んだ当の本人が、今それを証明して
いる。

　まさか……自分の列車が渡り終えた後で、橋を破壊
しようとでも云うのだろうか。
　それには相当量の爆弾、あるいは砲門が必要となる
筈だが、そんなものは影も形も見えない。

　わからなかった。
　……わからぬままに、俺は忍び寄る破滅の足音だけ
を聞いている。

　先行車が橋を渡り終えた。
　入れ違いに、<ruby>後続<rt>こちら</rt></ruby>が橋へ近付く。

　何も起こらない。
　雪車町は何もしない。

　ただ軽く、腕を上げて。
　空に――――
